newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's Napocor to sign power pact with Shell, Oxy.
newsitem.headline: Manila's Napocor to sign power pact with Shell, Oxy.

text.p: The Philippines Department of Energy said the National Power Corp (Napocor) will sign an agreement early next year for the purchase of power from a joint venture of Occidental Philippines Inc (Oxy) and Shell Philippines Exploration B.V.
Energy Minister Francisco Viray told reporters late on Friday that he is confident the power agreement will be finalised in the first quarter of 1997.
The two companies, units of Occidental Petroleum and Royal Dutch/Shell Group, have proposed converting a 620-MW mothballed nuclear power plant into a 1,500-MW gas-fired power plant.
Viray said he expects that a gas supply and purchase agreement will also be signed in the first quarter of next year.
Oxy and Shell are developers of the Camago-Malampaya gas field offshore southwestern Philippines, the biggest gas find which is scheduled to start production by the year 2001.

The mothballed Bataan Nuclear Power Plant will run on Camago-Malampaya gas. Negotiations for both the gas and power agreements resumed in September this year after being stalled by disagreements over the contract period and the markets for the gas.
The Bataan nuclear plan was built but never commissioned because of a dispute between the government and the builders, Westinghouse Electric and Burns & Roe.
